explainer_content.short_definition: Black sacred song and gospel-soul crossover where testimony, choir response, and vocal fire shape the route.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Mahalia Jackson, Sister Rosetta Tharpe, Aretha Franklin, the Staple Singers, Kirk Franklin, and peers connect church music to soul and modern gospel crossover.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It is one of the central roots of American popular singing, carrying religious function, civil-rights memory, and soul vocabulary.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The record often sounds like a congregation is implied, even when the arrangement is solo, soul, or contemporary gospel.
